title: Saved connection renewal
blurb: Mail and calendar renew saved connections as needed while Morrow is open. Gmail API mail sessions reread the saved connection for each request and can renew a rejected read once. Calendar and provider-feature reads can renew a rejected read once before offering reauthorization. Calendar quota errors pause feature reads before retry; they do not require new consent. A temporary Google client configuration problem keeps saved connections available when the same client is restored. Sends, draft saves and other writes are never replayed automatically. Outlook sync checks the saved connection before connecting and can renew a rejected login once, before any mailbox operation. Temporary network, sign-in-service and secure-storage failures keep the saved grant for retry, without marking the mailbox as needing sign-in. Renewed tokens must be saved before use; an omitted replacement refresh token preserves the previous one. Expired or revoked grants and provider interaction requirements need Reconnect for the affected mailbox or feature. Google External projects in Testing issue seven-day refresh tokens for mail and calendar. Production publishing and verification need the app owner's review; local readiness does not inspect them. Microsoft organization policies can require earlier sign-in. Changing the Google Desktop client still needs separate Gmail and Calendar reauthorization. Native secure-storage prompts and live provider policy are not verified by synthetic tests.
